decisions: A MODULE-LEVEL CONST THAT READS THE CLOCK IS A BUG, NOT A CACHE. CURRENT_MONTH_KEY was computed once at module load and never again, so it did not roll over at a month boundary at all - stale for the lifetime of a client session, and for the lifetime of the process wherever it was evaluated server-side. The UTC skew was the smaller half; unbounded staleness was the bigger one. Anything that answers 'what is now' must be a FUNCTION.

MONTH_KEY IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A LABEL. v_commissions_monthly attributes specials, adjustments AND the bonus to a month by exact string match (month_key = to_char(month,'YYYY-MM')), and v_driver_payslip_basis reads through it - so a wrong key files real money against the wrong month in Reports and on the wrong payslip. The 'month_key is kept only as a human label' comment on setCommissionBonus describes that upsert's CONFLICT TARGET (driver_id alone) and is not a statement about the views. Do not read it as one.

THE FIX WAS SCOPED TO THE CLOCK, NEVER THE MATH. currentMonthKey decides which month a write is filed under; it does not touch how any figure is computed. scripts/commission-rows-check.ts still reports ALL PASS, which is the standing proof that commission math is unchanged.

COMPOSED FROM EXISTING HELPERS: monthKeyOf(todayKey()). lib/commission-rows.ts previously had ZERO imports, and the one added is a deliberate leaf (lib/utils) so the module still runs directly under scripts/commission-rows-check.ts - verified by running it, not assumed.

EVERY DATE-KEY COMPARISON PUTS BOTH SIDES ON ONE CLOCK. toISOString().slice(0,10) is a UTC day and slice(0,7) a UTC month; trip_date, expected_return_on and every DATE column here are local calendar terms. Mixing them is correct for 21 hours a day, which is exactly why five instances survived multiple review passes.

NO NEW DATE HELPERS ANYWHERE IN THIS SWEEP. Everything routes through todayKey()/daysAgoKey() in lib/utils.ts. today+7 is daysAgoKey(-7) - negative n is the existing helper's own arithmetic, proven under TZ=Asia/Riyadh across month and year rollovers.

MIGRATIONS ARE COMMITTED THE MOMENT THE APPLY IS CONFIRMED (the db-reset rule), and the apply is VERIFIED rather than taken on report. 0120's anon check was the one that mattered: Supabase default privileges re-grant anon on every newly created relation and a REVOKE does not survive a DROP, so the restated footer was enforcement, not ceremony. It held - 40 views, 40 invoker, 0 anon-readable.
